subject.title: [Feature]: Expose an inbound non-message event hook to external channel plugins (e.g. reactions)

question: Should external channel plugins get a new public non-message event contract, or should OpenClaw bless an existing system-event/inbound-runner pattern for reactions, edits, typing, presence, and read receipts?
rationale: The current code has partial primitives but no documented external-channel contract, and choosing a new plugin SDK surface affects third-party compatibility and overlaps with the open inbound_activity PR.

options.title: Define a narrow SDK event contract
options.body: Add a versioned plugin-facing event adapter or runEvent-style dispatch surface with documented event kinds and regression tests for external channel plugins.

options.title: Bless existing primitives in docs
options.body: Document the exact system-event or inbound.run recipe for non-message channel activity and defer new API code until a plugin proves the recipe insufficient.

options.title: Defer until PR direction settles
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical API-direction thread while maintainers decide whether the related inbound_activity PR should be generalized, narrowed, or closed.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow SDK event contract
recommendation.body: Add a versioned plugin-facing event adapter or runEvent-style dispatch surface with documented event kinds and regression tests for external channel plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history on the plugin SDK/channel seam that would become the public compatibility boundary.
